verses.text: After this, Jesus showed himself to the disciples again by the Sea of Tiberias. Here’s how it happened.
Simon Peter, Thomas (also called Didymus), Nathanael from Cana in Galilee, the sons of Zebedee, and two other disciples were together.
Simon Peter said, “I’m going fishing.” They said, “We’re coming too.” They went out, got into the boat, and fished all night—but caught nothing.
When morning came, Jesus was standing on the shore, but the disciples didn’t recognize him.
Jesus called out, “Friends, have you caught anything to eat?” They answered, “No.”
He said, “Throw the net on the right side of the boat, and you’ll find some.” They did, and caught so many fish they couldn’t haul the net in.
The disciple Jesus loved said to Peter, “It’s the Lord!” When Simon Peter heard that, he pulled on his outer garment—he had taken it off—and jumped into the sea.
The other disciples came in the small boat, dragging the net full of fish. They weren’t far from shore—about two hundred cubits away.
When they got onto land, they saw a charcoal fire with fish cooking on it, and some bread.
Jesus said, “Bring some of the fish you just caught.”
Simon Peter went over and hauled the net ashore. It was full of 153 big fish. Even with that many, the net had not torn. 🐟
Jesus said, “Come have breakfast.” None of the disciples dared ask, “Who are you?” They knew it was the Lord.
Jesus came over, took the bread, and gave it to them. He did the same with the fish.
This was the third time Jesus showed himself to his disciples after rising from the dead.
After breakfast, Jesus asked Simon Peter, “Simon, son of Jonah, do you love me more than these?” Peter answered, “Yes, Lord. You know I care for you.” Jesus said, “Feed my lambs.”
Jesus asked him a second time, “Simon, son of Jonah, do you love me?” Peter answered, “Yes, Lord. You know I care for you.” Jesus said, “Take care of my sheep.”

Jesus asked him a third time, “Simon, son of Jonah, do you care for me?” Peter was hurt that Jesus had asked him a third time, “Do you care for me?” He answered, “Lord, you know everything. You know I care for you.” Jesus said, “Feed my sheep.

I’m telling you the truth: when you were young, you dressed yourself and went wherever you wanted. But when you’re old, you’ll stretch out your hands, and someone else will dress you and take you where you don’t want to go.”
Jesus said this to show the kind of death by which Peter would glorify God. Then he told him, “Follow me.”
Peter turned around and saw the disciple Jesus loved following them—the same one who had leaned against Jesus at supper and asked, “Lord, who is going to betray you?”
Peter saw him and asked Jesus, “Lord, what about him?”
Jesus answered, “If I want him to stay until I come, what’s that to you? You follow me.”
So word spread among the believers that this disciple wouldn’t die. But Jesus hadn’t said he wouldn’t die. He had said, “If I want him to stay until I come, what’s that to you?”
This is the disciple who testifies about these things and wrote them down. We know his testimony is true.
Jesus did many other things too. If every one of them were written down, I don’t think the whole world could hold all the books that would be written.
